correctness.rationale: Equations (1),(2) are derived by testing each current bit and both behavior types at every possible total-ones level, including tie boundaries; macro cycles, balanced 2cycles, fixed central layers and entire first-entry populations are then counted exhaustively symbolically. The proof handles all m,k>=1,N>=3 and sharpness. An independent vertexwise exhaustive finite check on all 104 type splits with 3<=N<=15 confirms each count; finite tests are not the all-N proof.

originality.rationale: The already published even balanced census is explicitly credited and excluded from the novelty claim; new structure concerns unbalanced populations and odd-order tie retention, where the 4cycle shifts to contrarian excess one and fixed equilibria become isolated. Haslegrave/Cannings supply period restrictions, not the all-parameter census. Cannings 2009 original complete paper was inaccessible and remains a significant historical-priority risk; no conclusive uniqueness assertion is made. Cao and Yang 2014 Theorem 5 establishes the fixed-point existence boundary under the same model, which is prior and explicitly credited; exact counts and basins remain extra.
residual_risks: Cannings 2009 primary full text specifically concerns complete-graph conformist/contrarian dynamics; formula overlap beyond cited period restrictions remains unresolved because the whole article was not accessible.
A prior result under equivalent behavioral-game terminology might be absent from indexed sources.
No independent expert priority review has been carried out.

value.rationale: The exact two-parameter all-size dynamical census determines a natural evolution invariant under heterogeneous majority/minority response. It reveals a sharp even/odd shift of unique 4cycle boundary and a contrarian-dominant odd regime with binomially many equilibrium states having singleton predecessor fibers, along with the sharp universal 2-step transient clock; these are substantive structural thresholds not routine numerical samples.
